cards.name: START HERE — Sprint 2 goal and Supabase scope
cards.description:
Sprint 2: one-week forecast for four members. Goal: a student can create an account, sign in, browse and filter inventory, and save a valid Pending request in Supabase; an authorized admin can read it.

Current decision (2026-11-20): Supabase Auth + PostgreSQL replace the earlier Firebase backend plan. Account creation is included again. React pages are reused; this board rework does not implement or migrate code.

Included: registration, confirmation state, session lifecycle, student/admin access rules, seeded inventory reads, search/filter states, validated request submission and admin Pending details.

Deferred: approval/allocation, pickup, returns, business email, calendar, audit export and image uploads. Picture metadata definitions remain in the database design; storage/upload use stays deferred for budget reasons.

Capacity: preliminary estimates are planning assumptions, not measured velocity. No calendar deadline is invented. See the five-day sequence and Definition of Done cards.

Existing Sprint 1 completion is preserved. New cards start in To Do; the team moves them only after checking actual branch/PR evidence. Older database design remains historical evidence, not proof that Supabase migration is complete.

Planning reference: https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html
Auth reference: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth
Access-policy reference: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security

cards.name: How cards move — entry rules and work limits
cards.description:
This board uses sprint planning with visible work states. These column names and WIP limits are team working agreements, not mandatory Scrum terminology.

Product Backlog: ordered future outcomes. Refine scope, acceptance checks, dependencies and estimate before selecting work.
Current Sprint [2] — To Do: selected Sprint 2 work. Pull a card when its inputs/contract are ready; fixtures may support development but never replace final live-data checks.
In Progress [2]: at most one active implementation per person, four total. Finish or help review before starting another card.
Review & Test [2]: at most two cards waiting. Add the PR, verification steps and known limitations; another member checks acceptance against the actual branch and development Supabase project.
Blocked [2]: use only for a real impediment. Put the blocker, required input, next action and responsible person in the description; discuss it daily and return the same card to its previous state when unblocked.
Done [2]: integrated changes that satisfy the shared Definition of Done. Prototype-only success does not complete a persistence or authorization card.
Sprint 1 — Completed: historical design work, not an implementation queue.
User Stories — Reference: parent goals; actionable work lives in the backlog/sprint.

Owner names in new-card descriptions are proposals based on existing team responsibilities. Existing card memberships are preserved. Each member should assign themselves to the cards they pull; the connector used for this rework does not expose native card-member assignment.

Keep the S2 identifier when a card moves. If scope changes, record the change and update dependencies rather than opening a duplicate.

cards.name: Definition of Done — reviewed, integrated and evidenced
cards.description:
A card reaches Done only when:

- Its acceptance checklist is complete and the final behavior matches the stated scope.
- A teammate has reviewed the PR/change and it has been integrated into the agreed branch.
- Build/lint and relevant behavior tests pass; record commands/results and the tested commit.
- Persistence/access-control cards are checked against development Supabase with ordinary user sessions; mocks alone do not prove them complete.
- Loading, rejected input, unavailable data and retry states relevant to the card have been checked.
- Schema changes include versioned SQL/migration notes and seed/setup instructions. No privileged credentials or real personal data are committed.
- The card links its PR/commit, evidence and any agreed limitation. Follow-up work receives a separate backlog card.

Ready to start: owner, small outcome, acceptance checks, estimate, dependency/input availability and review plan are understood. Split a card when its implementation cannot be reviewed in manageable steps.

For this sprint, sending actual lab notifications, paid storage, loan allocation and return processing are excluded. Accounts and Pending requests must be real Supabase-backed states.

Do not retroactively reinterpret completed Sprint 1 wireframes as shipped features. The older database-design completion covers a design artifact only.

cards.name: Sprint 2 — five-day sequence and capacity forecast
cards.description:
Timebox: one working week, four members. No calendar dates or due dates were invented. These initial estimates total 12 person-days and must be adjusted to actual coursework availability.

Proposed ownership:
- JD: S2-02 to S2-05 — Supabase service/schema and registration (3 person-days).
- Marc: S2-06 to S2-08 and S2-15 — sessions, routing, access checks and admin reads (3.25 person-days).
- Ethan: S2-01, S2-09, S2-10 and review coordination S2-16 (2.75 person-days).
- Iven: S2-11 to S2-14 — draft, validation and durable request submission (3 person-days).

Day 1 — planning and foundation: confirm capacity, registration/confirmation settings, date/quantity rules and access path; start client setup, shared Supabase service and schema/seed contract. Teammates can prepare UI states against that contract.
Day 2 — identity and data: complete profile/registration and schema policies; integrate sessions and inventory reads; prepare the booking draft.
Day 3 — student flow: complete login/role states, policy checks, search/filtering and form validation; begin the atomic save operation.
Day 4 — integration: save real Pending requests, verify safe retries and admin read-through; resolve cross-feature mismatches.
Day 5 — review/fixes: run S2-16, demonstrate the sprint goal, fix acceptance failures and hold a retrospective. Keep spare capacity for integration instead of pulling future features.

Daily: spend up to 15 minutes checking progress toward the goal, reviewing blocked work and planning the next actions; review waiting cards before starting more work.

Capacity rule: if the team cannot supply roughly three focused person-days per member, renegotiate scope during planning. Do not promise all 16 cards just because they exist. Preserve the agreed goal and quality; keep unselected/later work in Product Backlog.

At the next sprint: retain completed work as sprint history, return unfinished outcomes to the ordered Product Backlog with remaining acceptance checks, and create the next sprint goal/forecast.

cards.name: Sprint 2 review & retrospective — record actual outcomes
cards.description:
Use this card for the end-of-sprint record; it is not a claim that a review has happened.

Sprint review agenda:
- Demonstrate registration/confirmation handling, login, real inventory search/filtering and a saved Pending request.
- Open that same record as the provisioned admin and prove student isolation.
- Record the tested commit/project, completed outcome IDs, stakeholder feedback and remaining limitations.
- Move only genuinely accepted work to Done. Reorder unfinished/new work in Product Backlog with the team.

Retrospective agenda:
- What helped us finish and review work?
- What caused waiting, merge conflicts or failed integration?
- Choose one measurable improvement, an owner and a follow-up date agreed by the team.

Fill in after the event:
Review held: not yet recorded.
Demo/evidence link: not yet recorded.
Feedback and decisions: not yet recorded.
Retrospective improvement/owner: not yet recorded.

Process reference: https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html

Scope:
Allocate available quantities and save an admin decision in Supabase. Use the existing prototype as UI reference, not as proof of persistence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Only an authorized admin can approve a still-Pending request; at least one valid allocation is required.

- The decision, allocations, reviewer, timestamp and remarks are durable and visible after reload; repeated actions cannot apply twice.

cards.description:
Outcome: Empty Supabase schema → constrained tables, policies and seed

Owner: JD
Sprint: 2 | Priority: Must | Initial estimate: 1 person-day(s), to validate in planning | Target: day 1–2 of the five-day sequence
Parent: Enabler
Dependencies: S2-02

Scope:
Version the minimum SQL schema for profiles, inventory items, request headers and request lines. Include item-picture metadata and nullable user profile-picture metadata links, without storage buckets or upload UI. Preserve the old design as historical context.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repeatable migrations define auth-user ownership, protected student/admin roles, foreign keys, unique student IDs, timestamps and request/item identifiers.
- The quantity and unit contract covers whole equipment/disposables and fixed-precision chemicals; migration/adapters handle the previous quantityScale representation once, with no 100× display errors.
- RLS defaults to denial; students can read active inventory and their own requests, while only verified admins can read the queue. Students cannot promote themselves or change inventory/decision fields.
- A safe seed supplies equipment, chemicals, a zero-stock item and an inactive item; no real personal data or uploaded pictures are required.
- The schema supports atomic request-header/lines creation and a per-user unique submission key; migration instructions and the reviewed data contract are linked.

Scope:

- Retrying the same submission key after a lost response resolves to the original saved request and cannot insert duplicates.
- Verification covers network failure, expired session, changed stock and committed-but-response-lost retry.
